evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with metacresol medium containing metacresol (3 mg/mL) and glycerol (16 mg/mL); glycerol tested alone was negative.
evidence.support_text: Patch testing was positive to the metacresol medium containing metacresol (3 mg/mL) and glycerol (16 mg/mL); glycerol tested alone was negative. The patient had a Type IV hypersensitivity reaction to metacresol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with nitroglycerin solution or ointment.
evidence.support_text: The paper states that the majority of case reports describe allergic contact dermatitis to nitroglycerin and that the majority of cases had positive patch tests to nitroglycerin solution or ointment.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with NTG solution or ointment; patient used Nitradisc 10 transdermal system (2001, ref 16).
evidence.support_text: In a case reported in 2001 (reference 16), a patient using Nitradisc 10 developed erythema multiforme and had a positive patch test reaction to nitroglycerin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with NTG solution or ointment; patient was on transdermal NTG and i.v. isosorbide (2003, ref 15).
evidence.support_text: In a 2003 case (reference 15), a patient using transdermal NTG and i.v. isosorbide had a positive patch test to nitroglycerin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with NTG solution or ointment; patient was receiving i.v. isosorbide (2003, ref 15).
evidence.support_text: In a 2003 case (reference 15), a patient receiving i.v. isosorbide had a positive patch test to nitroglycerin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test with PCMC; concentration not specified; reading after 1 day (twice daily applications reported)
evidence.support_text: A 40-year-old male with severe hand and face dermatitis while using a sorbolene cream tested strongly positive to PCMC in patch testing after twice daily applications for 1 day (MacKenzie-Wood and Freeman 1997).

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test with Prolene® suture material
evidence.support_text: We report an allergic reaction to Prolene® sutures that has been confirmed by a positive patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with standard European series and additional substances; concentration of lidocaine not specified.
evidence.support_text: Patch tests to an extended European standard series, plus Anaesthesin 20% ointment and its ingredients, showed negative reactions to other local anaesthetics including lidocaine.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with tetrazepam; no concentration or vehicle specified.
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with various drugs that she had dealt with showed positivity only to tetrazepam. This case illustrates that sensitization can develop after only minor, though recurrent, exposures to tetrazepam.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with the face mask as a whole (test material)
evidence.support_text: The mask itself was negative on patch testing, indicating no allergic reaction to the mask as a whole.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test; no further details provided in the paper
evidence.support_text: In paragraph 232, the paper states: 'The patch test reaction to pentylene glycol in our patient was clearly allergic and clinically relevant.' This indicates a positive allergic contact dermatitis reaction to pentylene glycol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch tested as an ingredient of Anaesthesin® ointment and separately.
evidence.support_text: Other ingredients of the ointment, such as myristyl myristate, polysorbate 80, and softisan 649, and other local anaesthetics, such as lidocaine, bupivacaine, and procaine, were all negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch tested as part of a standard and medicaments series; positive reaction on day 4.
evidence.support_text: The patient was patch-tested to a standard and medicaments series of allergens and there was a positive (+) reaction to ethylenediamine on D4. Tests in 10 controls were entirely negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch tested as part of a standard and medicaments series; reading on day 4 (D4). Concentration not specified.
evidence.support_text: The patient was patch-tested to a standard and medicaments series of allergens and showed a positive (+) reaction to ethylenediamine on D4.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch tested in 2 cases
evidence.support_text: N,N-dimethylacrylamide (DMAA) was patch tested in two patients with negative results, indicating no skin sensitization response to this compound in the tested individuals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch tested on the upper back with the topical ophthalmic solution Diopine®; readings at D2 and D4.
evidence.support_text: Patch tests with European series were negative, whereas the patch test with Diopine® was positive (++) at D2 and D4, which was considered to be clinically relevant.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch tested with a standard series at standard concentrations; readings at D2 and D4.
evidence.support_text: Patch testing showed a positive reaction to methylhydroquinone (+), indicating a skin sensitization response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch testing in cement workers; specific concentrations and vehicles not reported in text
evidence.support_text: A high proportion of dichromate sensitization was seen in these workers, based on patch testing, indicating positive skin sensitization for dichromate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch testing with 2% 2-PE; irritancy threshold patch testing
evidence.support_text: Irritancy threshold patch testing was positive for 2% 2-PE in an 18-month-old infant with a strong family history of allergic reactions who developed eczema following DTaP vaccination containing 2-PE (Infanrix).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch testing with 5% idoxuridine in DMSO and 1% idoxuridine in DMSO; DMSO alone used as negative control.
evidence.support_text: One patient suffered acute local skin sensitization and showed a positive reaction to patch testing with idoxuridine 5% and 1% in DMSO but not with DMSO alone.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch testing with Efudix cream (as is, containing 11.5% PG) on a 56-year-old male patient.
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with Efudix cream (as is) produced a positive (++) allergic reaction in a 56-year-old male patient. The patient had been previously sensitized to PG in Unguentum M.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch testing with MIT in various concentrations (not specified in source); patients had prior exposure to MIT-containing products
evidence.support_text: Multiple case reports described positive patch test reactions to MIT in patients with allergic contact dermatitis from various exposures, including coolant solutions, moist toilet paper, and occupational settings, with reaction grades 2+ to +++.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch testing with the intact face mask material.
evidence.support_text: Patch testing of the face mask itself was negative, indicating no skin sensitization reaction to the mask material.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch testing with tumescent local anesthetic solution containing prilocaine 0.065% with adrenaline and methylhydroxybenzoat, and with lidocaine; patient had acute skin changes at time of testing; testing performed despite florid skin changes.
evidence.support_text: Epikutantestung durchgeführt, die eine Kontaktsensibilisierung gegen die verwendete Tumeszenz-LA-Lösung und gegen Lidocain zeigte. Aufgrund der Gruppenallergie mit Lidocain gehen wir davon aus, dass die relevante Kontaktsensibilisierung in der Tumeszenz-LA-Lösung gegen Prilocain gerichtet war.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch testing with various drugs dealt with by patient; positivity only to tetrazepam.
evidence.support_text: A geriatric nurse who crushed tetrazepam tablets developed periorbital dermatitis that spread to the whole face. Patch testing with various drugs she handled showed positivity only to tetrazepam.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch testing with various drugs; the patient was a geriatric nurse with occupational exposure to tetrazepam.
evidence.support_text: In a case of occupational airborne allergic contact dermatitis in a geriatric nurse, patch testing with various drugs showed positivity only to tetrazepam, indicating tetrazepam-induced allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patient tested with European standard, preservative, vehicle, plasticizer and glue, clothing and dye series and samples of gloves; readings at D2 and D4.
evidence.support_text: The patient had positive patch test reactions to ethylene urea melamine formaldehyde (EUMF) (+) at both D2 and D4.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patients sensitized to isoeugenol; unspecified esters
evidence.support_text: Patients sensitized to isoeugenol reacted to esters of isoeugenol in patch testing, attributed to cross-reactions or metabolism of esters in the skin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse epidermal JB6 cells; treatment with 8-hydroxy-α-humulene
evidence.support_text: 8-Hydroxy-α-humulene, a structural analogue of zerumbone that lacks the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl group, was unable to increase HO-1 expression as reported in the abstract.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse epidermal JB6 cells; treatment with α-humulene
evidence.support_text: α-Humulene, a structural analogue of zerumbone that lacks the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl group, was unable to increase HO-1 expression as reported in the abstract.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse epidermal JB6 cells; zerumbone treatment
evidence.support_text: Treatment of mouse epidermal JB6 cells with zerumbone caused a marked increase of the promoter activity of HO-1 as reported in the abstract.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse epidermal JB6 cells; zerumbone treatment
evidence.support_text: Treatment of mouse epidermal JB6 cells with zerumbone caused a marked increase of Nrf2 nuclear translocation as reported in the abstract.

evidence.assay_type: electrophoretic mobility shift assay or chromatin immunoprecipitation
evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse epidermal JB6 cells; zerumbone treatment
evidence.support_text: Treatment of mouse epidermal JB6 cells with zerumbone enhanced direct binding of Nrf2 to the antioxidant response element as reported in the abstract.

evidence.experimental_conditions: JB6 cells; details in Shin et al., 2011
evidence.support_text: Zerumbone from tropical ginger induced HO-1 and protected from ROS accumulation in JB6 and topical application mouse skin (Shin et al., 2011).

evidence.experimental_conditions: topical application onto dorsal skin of hairless mice; HO-1 protein levels measured in skin
evidence.support_text: Topical application of zerumbone onto dorsal skin of hairless mice induces heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) expression. In Nrf2 wild-type mice, HO-1 protein was detected, while Nrf2 knockout mice expressed much less HO-1 after zerumbone treatment.

evidence.experimental_conditions: HR-1 hairless mouse skin, topical application of zerumbol, Western blot
evidence.support_text: Only zerumbone, but not its nonelectrophilic analogue zerumbol, induced HO-1 expression in mouse skin in vivo (Figure 5F).

evidence.experimental_conditions: HR-1 hairless mouse skin, topical application of α-humulene, Western blot
evidence.support_text: Only zerumbone, but not its nonelectrophilic analogue α-humulene, induced HO-1 expression in mouse skin in vivo (Figure 5F).

evidence.experimental_conditions: HR-1 hairless mouse skin, topical zerumbone application, time- and dose-dependent, skin lysates analyzed by Western blot
evidence.support_text: Topical application of zerumbone to HR-1 hairless mouse skin induced HO-1 expression in a time-dependent and dose-dependent manner as shown by Western blot (Figure 3A and 3B).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Nude mice; topical zerumbone 55 or 110 µg/day in 50 µL PEG; 14 days with UVA 15 J/cm² every two days; skin homogenates
evidence.support_text: Nude mice treated topically with zerumbone (55 or 110 µg/day in 50 µL PEG) for 14 days with UVA exposure (15 J/cm² every two days) showed increased HO-1 protein expression in skin tissue homogenates by Western blot (positive).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Nude mice; topical zerumbone 55 or 110 µg/day in 50 µL PEG; 14 days with UVA 15 J/cm² every two days; skin homogenates
evidence.support_text: Nude mice treated topically with zerumbone (55 or 110 µg/day in 50 µL PEG) for 14 days with UVA exposure (15 J/cm² every two days) showed increased γ-GCLC protein expression in skin tissue homogenates by Western blot (positive).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Nrf2 knockout mouse dorsal skin, topical zerumbone, Western blot and immunohistochemistry
evidence.support_text: Zerumbone failed to induce HO-1 expression in the epidermis of Nrf2 knockout (−/−) mice (Figure 4A and 4B).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Nrf2 wild-type mouse dorsal skin, topical zerumbone, Western blot and immunohistochemistry
evidence.support_text: Topically applied zerumbone induced the expression of HO-1 in the epidermis of Nrf2 wild-type (+/+) mice, as shown by Western blot and immunohistochemistry (Figure 4A and 4B).

evidence.assay_type: Western blot of skin tissue lysates
evidence.experimental_conditions: HR-1 hairless mice, topical application of 10 µmol zerumbone in 200 µL acetone on dorsal skin for 6 hours; tissue lysates analyzed by Western blot
evidence.support_text: HR-1 hairless mice were treated topically with 10 µmol of zerumbone dissolved in 200 µL of acetone on the dorsal skin for 6 hours. Tissue lysates were prepared, and the levels of HO-1 expression were determined by Western blot analysis, showing induction of HO-1 compared to 0-hour control.

evidence.experimental_conditions: ROAT with 0.3% oxidized linalool (hydroperoxide content 564 µg/g, 0.056%), applied twice daily for 3 weeks at 10 mg/cm2 per application, resulting in 5.64 µg/cm2 per application. Patients were sensitized individuals exposed simultaneously to other formulations.
evidence.support_text: The ROAT with 0.3% oxidized linalool (hydroperoxide 564 µg/g, 0.056%) gave a LOEL for elicitation at a dose per area of 5.64 µg/cm2, corresponding to elicitation in sensitized patients (Table 1, row 5; footnote g).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Incubation with homogenate of human melanoma cells, 30 min, without L-dopa cofactor
evidence.support_text: Incubation of TBC with homogenate of human melanoma cells (without L-dopa cofactor) resulted in about 65% TBC consumption after 30 min, along with formation of a small amount of TBQ and dark violet color indicating quinone oligomerization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Incubation with homogenate of human melanoma cells, L-cysteine present, L-dopa cofactor, 10 min
evidence.support_text: Incubation of TBC with homogenate of human melanoma cells in the presence of L-cysteine and L-dopa cofactor resulted in 50% TBC consumption after 10 min and the formation of cys-TBC, identified by HPLC comparison.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Immortalized human keratinocyte cell line HaCaT, treated with MeDHICA-melanin at 10 µg/mL, UVA irradiation
evidence.support_text: In the abstract, the authors report that MeDHICA-melanin, a polymer prepared by aerial oxidation of the methyl ester of DHICA (MeDHICA), at 10 µg/mL prevented reactive oxygen species accumulation and partially reduced glutathione oxidation in UVA-irradiated HaCaT keratinocytes. Western blot experiments revealed that the polymer induces the translocation of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf-2) to the nucleus with activation of transcription of antioxidant enzymes, such as heme-oxygenase 1.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Normal human epidermal keratinocytes (NHEKs) exposed to BaP (20 nM, 40 nM, 100 nM, 1 µM, 10 µM) for 3, 6, and 24 h; protein measured by Western blotting.
evidence.support_text: Western blotting analysis revealed that protein levels of CYP1A1 were up-regulated by BaP in a dose-dependent manner in NHEKs.

evidence.experimental_conditions: PAM 212 cells and primary mouse keratinocytes, 10-30 µM 4-HNE, 6-12 h
evidence.support_text: 4-HNE (10-30 µM) induced HO-1 protein expression maximally after 6-12 h in PAM 212 cells and primary mouse keratinocytes, as shown by western blotting.

evidence.experimental_conditions: PAM212 and primary WT mouse keratinocytes; 3 µM sulforaphane; treatment for 3 or 6 h in serum-free medium, then wash and refeed with growth medium; homogenates prepared after additional 24 h; Gapdh loading control
evidence.support_text: In PAM212 cells and primary keratinocytes, sulforaphane also increased protein expression of Ho-1 as shown by Western blotting after treatment with 3 µM sulforaphane.

evidence.experimental_conditions: PAM212 and primary WT mouse keratinocytes; 3 µM sulforaphane; treatment for 3 or 6 h in serum-free medium, then wash and refeed with growth medium; homogenates prepared after additional 24 h; Gapdh loading control
evidence.support_text: In PAM212 cells and primary keratinocytes, sulforaphane also increased protein expression of Nqo1 as shown by Western blotting after treatment with 3 µM sulforaphane.

evidence.assay_type: Western blot analysis of Keap1 redox forms
evidence.experimental_conditions: Human Keap1 expressed in cells, treatment with SFN, non-reducing electrophoresis, Western blot detection
evidence.support_text: Similar changes in Keap1 redox state were detected with human Keap1 in response to SFN and TNBS, although to a much lesser extent than with mouse Keap1.

evidence.assay_type: Western blot analysis of Keap1 redox forms
evidence.experimental_conditions: Human Keap1 expressed in cells, treatment with TNBS, non-reducing electrophoresis, Western blot detection
evidence.support_text: Similar changes in human Keap1 redox state were observed after TNBS treatment, although to a lesser extent than in mouse.

evidence.assay_type: Western blot analysis of Keap1 redox forms
evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse Keap1 expressed in cells, treatment with SFN, non-reducing electrophoresis, Western blot detection
evidence.support_text: Both SFN and TNBS decreased reduced mouse Keap1 when tested in cells expressing mouse Keap1 and treated with these compounds, as shown by non-reducing Western blotting. SFN specifically increased the formation of intramolecular disulfide-bonded Keap1, while TNBS increased intermolecular disulfide-bonded Keap1.

evidence.assay_type: Western blot analysis of Keap1 redox forms
evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse Keap1 expressed in cells, treatment with TNBS, non-reducing electrophoresis, Western blot detection
evidence.support_text: Both SFN and TNBS decreased reduced mouse Keap1. TNBS increased intermolecular disulfide-bonded Keap1, as detected by non-reducing Western blotting.

review_policy.eligible_subject: unique measurement-producing subject, donor, or cell-system species
